headlines.title: ConocoPhillips (COP) Stock Looks Like A Bargain On Its 184% Run
headlines.summary: ConocoPhillips stock has delivered very strong long term gains over the past five years, yet the broader valuation checks point to a mixed picture rather than a clear bargain or clear overvaluation at the current price. ConocoPhillips has returned 183.8% over the past five years, which sets a high bar for any further value the share price may offer.

headlines.title: ConocoPhillips (COP) Gives Finance Chief Role To Insider Kontessa Haynes Welsh
headlines.summary: ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) has appointed Kontessa S. Haynes-Welsh as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The leadership change reflects internal advancement within the existing ConocoPhillips executive team. The new CFO role places Haynes-Welsh at the center of the company’s financial planning, reporting and capital allocation decisions. Executive reshuffles like this often prompt investors to look more broadly at financially disciplined companies.

description: ConocoPhillips explores for, produces, transports, and markets crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG), and natural gas liquids. It operates in five segments: Alaska; Lower 48; Canada; Europe, Middle East and North Africa; and Asia Pacific. The company's portfolio includes unconventional plays in North America; conventional assets in North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia; global LNG developments; oil sands assets in Canada; and an inventory of global exploration prospects. It serves in the United States, Canada, China, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and internationally. ConocoPhillips was founded in 1917 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
